title: Sepsis, Septic Shock, and Inpatient Infection Management

steps.tx: A life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by a dysregulated, host-damaging immune response to an underlying infection is defined clinically as **sepsis**. Pathophysiologically, pathogen-associated molecular patterns (such as bacterial endotoxin lipopolysaccharide) trigger massive macrophage activation, systemic cytokine release, widespread endothelial glycocalyx degradation, microvascular permeability, and cellular metabolic dysoxia.
steps.say: A life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by a dysregulated host response to infection is defined as sepsis. Pathogen molecular patterns trigger macrophage activation, cytokine storms, endothelial barrier breakdown, microvascular leakage, and cellular metabolic impairment.

steps.tx: A critical subset of sepsis featuring profound cellular, metabolic, and circulatory abnormalities carrying hospital mortality exceeding forty percent is **septic shock**. Diagnostic criteria require persistent hypotension necessitating vasopressor infusions to maintain a mean arterial pressure of sixty-five mmHg or higher, accompanied by an elevated serum lactate exceeding two millimoles per litre despite adequate fluid resuscitation.
steps.say: A critical subset of sepsis featuring profound circulatory and metabolic failure with mortality exceeding forty percent is septic shock. Diagnostic criteria mandate persistent hypotension requiring vasopressors to maintain mean arterial pressure above sixty-five mmHg, along with elevated lactate despite fluid resuscitation.

steps.tx: Bedside identification of patients at heightened risk of in-hospital mortality utilizes the quick Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (**qSOFA**) bedside score. Calculating three objective bedside physiological parameters (Respiratory rate twenty-two breaths per minute or higher, Altered mental status with GCS under fifteen, Systolic blood pressure one-hundred mmHg or lower), a score of two or higher prompts urgent ICU evaluation.
steps.say: Bedside identification of high-risk sepsis patients utilizes the quick Sequential Organ Failure Assessment bedside tool. Scoring respiratory rate above twenty-two, altered mentation, and systolic pressure under one hundred, a score of two or higher prompts urgent clinical evaluation.

steps.tx: Formal quantification of sepsis organ dysfunction relies on the full **SOFA score**, evaluating six physiological systems: respiration (PaO2/FiO2 ratio), coagulation (platelet count), hepatic function (serum bilirubin), cardiovascular support (mean arterial pressure or required vasopressor dose), central nervous system (Glasgow Coma Scale), and renal function (serum creatinine or daily urine output).
steps.say: Formal quantification of sepsis organ dysfunction relies on the full SOFA score, evaluating six organ systems: respiration, platelet count, bilirubin, cardiovascular vasopressor requirements, Glasgow Coma Scale, and renal creatinine excretion.

steps.tx: Resuscitation bundles dictate the mandatory delivery of the hour-one sepsis bundle. Clinicians must measure baseline **serum lactate** (re-measuring within four hours if initial level exceeds two millimoles per litre), obtain two sets of peripheral blood cultures prior to antimicrobial initiation, administer broad-spectrum intravenous empirical antibiotics within one hour, and rapidly infuse thirty millilitres per kilogram of balanced crystalloids.
steps.say: Resuscitation protocols mandate delivering the hour-one sepsis bundle. Clinicians must measure serum lactate, draw blood cultures prior to antibiotics, administer broad-spectrum intravenous antimicrobials within one hour, and infuse thirty millilitres per kilogram of balanced crystalloid solution.

steps.tx: The absolute first-line vasopressor of choice in septic shock unresponsive to crystalloid volume resuscitation is continuous intravenous **noradrenaline** (norepinephrine). Noradrenaline delivers potent alpha-1 vascular vasoconstriction to restore systemic vascular resistance and mean arterial pressure alongside modest beta-1 inotropic support, titrating to maintain mean arterial pressure at sixty-five mmHg while minimising tachyarrhythmias.

steps.tx: Hospital-acquired infections frequently involve multidrug-resistant pathogens requiring specific antimicrobial coverage. Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) mandates glycopeptides (vancomycin) or lipopeptides (daptomycin). Gram-negative bacteria harbouring extended-spectrum beta-lactamases (**ESBL**) require carbapenems (meropenem), while carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CRE) require novel beta-lactamase inhibitor combinations such as ceftazidime-avibactam.

Gram-negative bacilli producing extended-spectrum beta-lactamases require meropenem, while carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales require ceftazidime-avibactam.

steps.tx: An acute oncological and infectious emergency presenting with an absolute neutrophil count falling under five-hundred cells per microlitre (or predicted decline below 500 within forty-eight hours) accompanied by a single temperature exceeding 38.3 degrees Celsius is **febrile neutropenia**. Empirical monotherapy with an antipseudomonal beta-lactam (intravenous piperacillin-tazobactam, cefepime, or meropenem) must be initiated within sixty minutes.
